---
title: "The model"
---

`LongRunRisksModel` is one economy and a set of named claims. The
economy is a consumption process and an Epstein-Zin investor. Each
claim is a cash-flow stream that loads on that process. The Euler
equation prices every claim in the set.

```python
import lrrcs as lrr

model = lrr.LongRunRisksModel()
res = model.solve()
print(res.summary())
```

With no arguments the specification is Kiku (2006), Table II. That
calibration includes three claims named `value`, `growth`, and
`market`.

## What the model takes as given

Preferences are $(\delta, \gamma, \psi)$. Consumption growth has a
small persistent component $x_t$ and a volatility component. A claim
has four cash-flow parameters. Across a cross-section the parameter
that changes the economics is $\phi$, the loading on $x_t$.

`ModelParams()`, `PreferencesParams`, `ConsumptionParams`, and
`ClaimParams` are the dataclasses. You rarely build them by hand.
Override one field on the model instead.

```python
lrr.LongRunRisksModel(gamma=7.5)
lrr.LongRunRisksModel(claims={"value": {"phi": 2.6}})
```

`.replace(...)` returns a new model. The original object is not
edited.

## What the model produces

`.solve()` and `.simulate()` return result objects with expected
returns, volatilities, Sharpe ratios, price-dividend ratios, and the
risk-free rate. Returns, premia, and rates are annualized and in
percent. Quantities that vary by claim are series indexed by claim
name.

The model does not know that one claim is "value". A spread is a
question you ask after the solve.

```python
res.compare("value", "growth", market="market").premium
```

`market` is only needed for CAPM betas. Any priced claim can be the
reference.

## Why expected cash-flows and the premium share a model

The risk premium is payment for the risk in the expected cash-flows.
It should depend on how expected cash-flows move when times are bad,
and on whether the investor already dislikes those times. Both
objects are readings of the same $\phi$.

The [API](../reference/api.qmd) lists every public name.
[Calibration](calibration.qmd) measures $\phi$ from cash-flows.
[Solution methods](solution.qmd) describes the grid, the
log-linear shortcut, and simulation.
